title: Java references instead of explicit pointers
answer: No. Java does not let ordinary source code declare C/C++-style pointer variables, use pointer declarators such as `int*`, perform pointer arithmetic, or explicitly dereference raw memory addresses. Java uses managed references for objects instead. A reference can refer to an object or be `null`, and Java lets you compare or pass references, but ordinary Java code does not expose the object's raw address for pointer arithmetic. APIs such as `WeakReference`, `SoftReference`, and `PhantomReference` are managed reference objects, not C-style pointers. Native-memory access is handled through specialized interop/runtime APIs rather than ordinary pointer syntax.

steps.title: Open Java's managed-reference example
steps.question: Java still needs a way for code to refer to objects even though the language does not expose C or C++ pointer syntax; In AeroTopo's RuntimeLab, the reference utilities use Java's managed reference APIs; What should you notice about these types before deciding whether Java has explicit pointers.
steps.why_te: RuntimeLab.java lo Java managed reference APIs kanipistayi; `WeakReference`, `SoftReference` mariyu `PhantomReference` objects ni refer chestayi; Kani avi C/C++ style raw pointers kaavu.

steps.question: The method parameter `Object point` receives a reference to an object, and Java code can pass that reference without receiving the object's raw address; Why is an object reference useful for normal programming while still being different from a pointer that exposes address arithmetic and manual dereferencing.
steps.why_te: `Object point` object ni refer chestundi; Method ki object access istundi, kani raw address ni expose cheyyadu; Java lo normal object references tho work chestam.

steps.title: Inspect WeakReference as a Java class

steps.why_te: IntelliJ symbol card lo `WeakReference` normal Java class ga kanipistundi; Idi garbage collector tho cooperate chese reference API; Raw pointer type la memory address arithmetic ivvadu.
